claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr suffers rapid oxidation or pesting in air.
A thin aluminide surface coating on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a protective alumina layer during high-temperature exposure.
The alumina-forming coating will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve the alloy's intrinsic mechanical properties.
Pack cementation or chemical vapor deposition can be used to produce the proposed aluminide coating.
The coating will produce a continuous, dense Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a diffusion barrier against oxygen ingress into the substrate.
At high temperature, the aluminide coating will react with ambient oxygen to form a stable alumina scale.
The alumina scale will minimize oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
Reduced oxygen diffusion will prevent pesting and oxidation-related degradation.
The coating and alumina scale will leave the substrate microstructure largely unaffected.
Under 800 °C air exposure for 5 hours, coated specimens will show significantly less oxide-scale growth than untreated specimens.
Under 800 °C air exposure for 5 hours, coated specimens will show less pesting than untreated specimens.
Coated specimens will retain room-temperature ductility comparable to untreated specimens.
Coated specimens will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to untreated specimens.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid pesting during a 5-hour exposure to air at about 800 °C.
Rapid oxidation of untreated material degrades its structural integrity and mechanical properties over time.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between coating and substrate may cause delamination or impair mechanical performance under cyclic conditions.
